source.note: Captures the OpenAI chat RequestFromLLM tool-filtering rule: a unified llm.Request carrying both a ToolTypeResponsesCustomTool and a ToolTypeFunction tool MUST yield an outbound OpenAI Request whose tools contain ONLY the function tool (length 1, type 'function', name 'get_weather'). This is a contract-level conversion case, not a full HTTP round-trip. inbound_http, selected_channel, upstream_http and client_http are null because the Go test does not exercise those stages — it only calls RequestFromLLM on a synthetic unified request.

unified_request._comment: Exact llm.Request literal passed to RequestFromLLM in the Go test (model 'gpt-4o', one user message 'hi', two tools).

outbound_http._comment: Expected OpenAI chat Request after RequestFromLLM filtering. Go test asserts req != nil, len(req.Tools)==1, req.Tools[0].Type==llm.ToolTypeFunction ('function'). The tool's function name 'get_weather' and parameters {"type":"object"} are copied from the input fixture (they survive the filter unchanged). Other request fields (model, messages) are passed through by RequestFromLLM and are copied verbatim from the Go input literal.
